note: Paragraphs View Modes ships a single Paragraphs behavior plugin, paragraphs_viewmode_behavior, with no settings form, no configure route (configure=null), no permissions, no Drush, and no plugin type of its own. Its only config is the behavior plugin settings on a paragraphs_type config entity: paragraphs.paragraphs_type.<type> -> behavior_plugins.paragraphs_viewmode_behavior with keys enabled, override_mode, override_available (map), override_default. The per-paragraph pick is a behavior setting named view_mode on the paragraph entity, applied at render via hook_entity_view_mode_alter(). Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config on a paragraphs_type.

evals.prompt: In Drupal, the paragraphs_viewmode module lets an editor choose a paragraph's view mode per instance. It has no admin settings page. How do you turn its feature on for a given paragraph type, and what is the machine name of the plugin involved?
evals.expected_output: You enable the Paragraphs behavior plugin paragraphs_viewmode_behavior on the paragraph type's edit form (Behaviors section). It is a paragraphs behavior plugin, not a field/formatter, and there is no configure route.

evals.prompt: For the paragraphs_viewmode behavior plugin, which configuration keys does it store on the paragraph type, and what does each control?
evals.expected_output: It stores override_mode (which rendered view mode triggers the swap), override_available (the map of view modes an editor may switch to), and override_default (the default choice, which must also be in override_available). They live under behavior_plugins.paragraphs_viewmode_behavior on the paragraphs.paragraphs_type.<type> config entity.

evals.prompt: How does the paragraphs_viewmode module actually change the view mode a paragraph is rendered with at display time? Name the Drupal hook it implements.
evals.expected_output: It implements hook_entity_view_mode_alter(): for a paragraph entity it calls the enabled behavior plugin's entityViewModeAlter(), which replaces the active view mode with the per-paragraph 'view_mode' behavior setting the editor chose.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, a paragraph type named pvm_known has the paragraphs_viewmode behavior enabled. Inspect the live configuration and state its default view mode (the override_default value).
evals.expected_output: override_default is 'teaser': in paragraphs.paragraphs_type.pvm_known the behavior_plugins.paragraphs_viewmode_behavior mapping has enabled: true and override_default: teaser.

evals.prompt: A paragraph type pvm_known exists on this site. Does it have the paragraphs_viewmode behavior (paragraphs_viewmode_behavior) enabled, and which view modes may an editor switch to for it? Inspect the live config to answer.
evals.expected_output: Yes, paragraphs_viewmode_behavior is enabled on pvm_known; override_available lists default and teaser, so an editor may switch between the default and teaser view modes.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a paragraph type pvm_task with no behaviors configured. Using the paragraphs_viewmode module, enable its behavior plugin on pvm_task so editors can switch a paragraph between the 'default' and 'teaser' view modes, with 'teaser' as the default. Apply the change to the live site config.
evals.expected_output: In paragraphs.paragraphs_type.pvm_task the behavior_plugins.paragraphs_viewmode_behavior mapping has enabled: true, override_available containing default and teaser, and override_default set to a value present in override_available (e.g. teaser).

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site I have a content block type called 'pvm_task' and I want editors to be able to pick, for each block they add, whether it shows in the normal layout or a shorter 'teaser' style, defaulting to the shorter one. Please set that up for me on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable the paragraphs_viewmode_behavior on the pvm_task paragraph type with override_available including default and teaser and override_default = teaser, saved to paragraphs.paragraphs_type.pvm_task.
